result.title: Reasoning for Propaganda Detection via Label-Guided CoT Optimisation
result.summary: Propaganda detection systems usually operate as black boxes, lacking explanations. To address this, we hypothesise that persuasive techniques contain definitional characteristics with respect to their social-political setting. We introduce ReCoT, a reasoning-conditioned detection framework that captures definitional cues of persuasive techniques via population-level refinement and performance-guided resampling, without requiring additional explanation annotations. On INDI-PROPspan, ReCoT achieves a macro F1_LCS of 0.364, surpassing baselines and reaching 88% of the SFT upper bound on Avg F1_LCS. Similarly, on PTC, ReCoT reaches 85% of the SFT upper bound on Avg F1_LCS, closing much of this gap while remaining interpretable. Importantly, the analysis of the reasoning pool's convergence and update pattern for ReCoT shows effective refinement of reasoning CoTs.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 ReCoT，一个 reasoning-conditioned 的 propaganda 检测框架，用群体级优化与 performance-guided resampling 在无解释标注条件下获得定义性线索，并在 INDI-PROPspan、PTC 上报告了相对基线与 SFT 上界的 F1_LCS 表现。
